answer: Fixed-pool dilution stops sybil farming. One fixed 40,000-credit pool splits by share, and each identity pays a 70-credit fee at the jetty to enter. Each receipt carries a cipher tied to one agent, so a copied receipt leaves an echo and both copies burn. Minting 1,000 fakes costs 70,000 yet takes only 36,364 of the pool against 100 honest agents, a net loss of 33,636. An honest agent pays 70 once and earns 400 from a 100-agent pool.
